title: Binary Trees and Traversals
summary: Trees as recursive structures - nodes, roots, leaves, depth and height, binary trees with unique_ptr children, writing functions recursively (size, height, mirror), the depth-first orders pre-, in- and post-order, doing them without recursion using an explicit stack, level-order traversal with a queue, rebuilding a tree from two traversals, and serialising a tree to text.

cards.q: What is the in-order traversal of a tree with root 2, left child 1 and right child 3?
Which traversal suits deleting every node of a tree safely?
cards.a:
post-order

Children are handled before their parent, so no node is deleted while its children still need it.

cards.q: Which data structure does level-order traversal use?
cards.a:
a queue

First in, first out: nodes are visited in the order they were discovered, level by level.
